claims.claim: AST SpaceMobile's company timeline records next-generation BlueBird 8-10 launches on June 17, 2026 and BlueBird 11-13 launches on August 5, 2026, following BlueBird 7 in April and BlueBird 6 in December 2025.

factors.name: direct-to-device constellation deployment
factors.basis: successive multi-satellite launches indicate the network is moving from demonstration toward constellation scale

risks.risk: Deployment progress does not by itself prove commercial service quality, regulatory coverage, unit economics or launch cadence durability.

causalEdges.mechanism: additional satellites increase orbital capacity and geographic/time coverage available to partner networks
causalEdges.falsifier: launched satellites fail commissioning or service coverage/capacity does not scale with deployment

unknowns.unknown: Current commercial revenue conversion, service-level performance and remaining constellation funding require underwriting.

claims.claim: AST SpaceMobile's 2026 quarterly-results page provides Q1 and Q2 earnings releases, presentations and Forms 10-Q, while the deployment timeline shows two multi-satellite launch events by August 2026.

factors.name: deployment execution
factors.basis: multiple next-generation satellites were launched across successive 2026 missions, providing observable execution against constellation buildout

risks.risk: Launch execution can outpace monetization; capital intensity and satellite commissioning remain material execution dependencies.

causalEdges.mechanism: constellation density is a prerequisite for broader continuous service
causalEdges.falsifier: launches continue but commercial coverage, capacity or partner monetization fails to progress

unknowns.unknown: Scout does not infer financial sufficiency or valuation from launch cadence; Alpha must underwrite Q2 financials and liquidity.
